questions.question: How did tethering affect programmed −1 frameshifting at the IS911, IS3, and dnaX sites when wild-type SD sequences were used?

options.A: Ribo-T retained similar efficiencies: 14% vs 13% for IS911, 33% for IS3 with either ribosome, and 45% vs 43% for dnaX
options.B: Ribo-T abolished all three events because it could not recognize wild-type SD sequences
options.C: Ribo-T selectively enhanced IS3 to 60%, while IS911 and dnaX fell below 5%
options.D: Ribo-T reduced each event by approximately half relative to wild type

questions.rationale: Despite the orthogonal anti-SD sequence, Ribo-T maintained near-wild-type −1 frameshifting on the tested signals, unlike its impaired +1 frameshifting.
questions.evidence_quote: the efficiency of -1 ribosomal frameshifting was 13% for IS911 with wild-type ribosomes and 14% with Ribo-T ribosomes (p-value of 0.54), 33% for IS3 with either type of ribosome (p-value of 0.77), 43% for dnaX with wild-type ribosomes and 45% with Ribo-T ribosomes

questions.question: What was the central +1 frameshifting result for Ribo-T on the E. coli prfB signal, and did replacing the SD sequence rescue it?

options.A: Ribo-T achieved only 2% versus 33% for wild type, and the Ribo-T-recognized SD did not restore activity (1.8%)
options.B: Ribo-T achieved 33% versus 2% for wild type, and the orthogonal SD reduced it to 0.6%
options.C: Both ribosomes achieved about 30%, and SD replacement increased Ribo-T to 45%
options.D: Ribo-T achieved 14%, and orthogonal SD replacement restored wild type to 44%

questions.rationale: The tethered ribosome is strongly impaired for +1 frameshifting, and changing to an SD it can recognize did not rescue the phenotype.
questions.evidence_quote: However, Ribo-T ribosomes frameshift inefficiently on this sequence, with an efficiency of only 2% (p-value of 8.9x10 -9 versus wild-type ribosomes

questions.question: How did the investigators calculate translational efficiency in their dual-reporter assay?

options.A: They normalized the target luciferase/β-galactosidase ratio to the corresponding in-frame construct and used medians from at least six independent experiments
options.B: They divided β-galactosidase activity by optical density and averaged three technical replicates
options.C: They measured luciferase alone relative to a no-SD background in one experiment per construct
options.D: They divided the target protein yield by mRNA abundance and normalized to cell growth rate

questions.rationale: The assay uses a dual-reporter normalization against the corresponding in-frame construct and reports median values from at least six independent experiments.
questions.evidence_quote: The translational efficiency of the ribosomes was calculated as the ratio of luciferase activity to β-galactosidase activity for the target, divided by the ratio of luciferase activity to βgalactosidase activity for the corresponding in-frame construct.

questions.question: What did the authors infer from the fourfold luciferase induction with the Ribo-T-specific SD sequence in the initiation reporter?

options.A: Ribo-T could use the orthogonal SD sequence, but less efficiently than wild-type ribosomes use the wild-type SD
options.B: Wild-type ribosomes preferred the orthogonal SD over their canonical SD
options.C: Ribo-T initiation was entirely SD-independent and the fourfold difference was caused by β-galactosidase
options.D: The orthogonal SD restored Ribo-T initiation to the wild-type level

questions.rationale: The Ribo-T-specific SD induced luciferase in the presence of Ribo-T, but this initiation was inefficient compared with wild-type ribosomes at a canonical SD.
questions.evidence_quote: Interestingly, in the presence of Ribo-T ribosomes, luciferase induction was increased by a factor of four (p-value 4.7x10 -4 ), indicating that Ribo-T ribosomes can use this alternative SD sequence, albeit inefficiently relative to WT ribosomes in the presence of a wild-type SD sequence

questions.question: What experiment argued against scanning as the route by which ribosomes initiated the downstream luc gene in the lacZ-luc reporter?

options.A: A stable stem-loop placed after lacZ did not affect luc initiation (p=0.22), supporting internal loading
options.B: Deleting the luc start codon did not affect β-galactosidase production
options.C: A stop codon was inserted before lacZ and increased luc initiation fourfold
options.D: Changing the upstream SD sequence abolished all luciferase activity

questions.rationale: A stable RNA structure would block scanning; its lack of effect on luc expression supports internal loading rather than scanning-mediated reinitiation.
questions.evidence_quote: We found that structure had no effect on the initiation of luc translation (p-value 0.22), strongly suggesting that the initiation of luc translation occurred through the internal loading of Ribo-T ribosomes

questions.question: How did Ribo-T perform in stop-codon recognition relative to wild-type ribosomes?

options.A: Readthrough was higher for Ribo-T at UAG, UGA, and UAA, consistent with less efficient termination
options.B: Readthrough was lower for Ribo-T at all three stop codons, indicating enhanced termination
options.C: Ribo-T differed only at UGA, while UAG and UAA were indistinguishable
options.D: Neither ribosome showed measurable readthrough for any tested stop codon

questions.rationale: The reported readthrough fractions were higher for Ribo-T than wild type for each stop codon, leading the authors to conclude termination is mildly impaired.
questions.evidence_quote: We found that Ribo-T ribosomes terminated translation less efficiently than wild-type ribosomes

questions.question: Which reporter design enabled the authors to distinguish initiation by wild-type from Ribo-T ribosomes?

options.A: They paired the wild-type SD upstream of lacZ with a mutated CACCAC SD complementary to Ribo-T's altered anti-SD for Ribo-T assays
options.B: They used a common wild-type SD for both ribosomes and separated them by antibiotic resistance
options.C: They inserted a fluorescent tag into the 16S rRNA and measured fluorescence during translation
options.D: They deleted both SD sequences and relied on different promoter strengths

questions.rationale: The altered SD sequence recruits Ribo-T selectively; in cells containing both ribosome types, only Ribo-T efficiently initiates at the orthogonal message.
questions.evidence_quote: For assessments of the translational efficiency of Ribo-T ribosomes, we used the corresponding constructs with a mutated SD sequence CACCAC upstream from the lacZ gene, in the presence of the vector encoding the Ribo-T ribosomes.

questions.question: What growth and protein-synthesis costs were associated with Ribo-T in the prior characterization cited by the authors?

options.A: Doubling time was 107 min rather than 35 min for wild type, and protein synthesis was 50% of wild-type rate
options.B: Doubling time was 35 min rather than 107 min, and protein synthesis doubled
options.C: Doubling time was unchanged, but protein synthesis fell to 2% of wild type
options.D: Doubling time was 50 min rather than 35 min, with equal protein-synthesis rates

questions.rationale: Tethered ribosomes support growth but have a slower-growth phenotype and reduced overall protein synthesis, attributed largely to slower biogenesis.
questions.evidence_quote: The resulting ribosome, Ribo-T, with its inseparable subunits, was shown to be functional and able to sustain the cell growth, although doubling times were slower (107 min for Ribo-T, 35 min for wild-type ribosomes).

questions.question: What structural explanation did the authors propose for the broad inefficiency of SD use by Ribo-T?

options.A: Tethering through helix 44 may alter the orientation of the anti-SD sequence, impairing its normal interactions
options.B: The tether deletes the 16S rRNA anti-SD sequence completely
options.C: The 23S rRNA binding pocket blocks the mRNA start codon from entering the A site
options.D: The orthogonal SD sequence is methylated and therefore cannot pair with any ribosome

questions.rationale: Because the tether links subunits through H44, the authors suggest altered H44 geometry could reorient the anti-SD and explain reduced SD use during initiation and elongation.
questions.evidence_quote: We therefore suggest that its orientation is modified in Ribo-T ribosomes, preventing them from using SD sequences in a normal manner during translation initiation and elongation.

questions.question: Which limitation did the authors identify as necessary to resolve the proposed H44-based explanation?

options.A: A high-resolution structure of Ribo-T ribosomes is needed to test the suggested anti-SD orientation change
options.B: A larger library of stop codons is needed because UAG, UGA, and UAA cannot measure termination
options.C: The assay must be repeated in yeast because bacterial ribosomes lack H44
options.D: The mutant ribosome must be purified from all cells before any reporter interpretation is possible

questions.rationale: The authors present altered anti-SD orientation as a proposal, and explicitly note structural work would be needed to resolve it.
questions.evidence_quote: The elucidation of a high-resolution structure for Ribo-T ribosomes would help to resolve this question.
